title: Cabral reaches Brazil
summary: A Portuguese fleet bound for India swings far west and lands in Brazil, which Portugal claims under the Treaty of Tordesillas.

title: Safavid dynasty founded in Iran
summary: Shah Ismail I takes Tabriz and makes Twelver Shia Islam the state religion of Iran — still the case today.

title: Leonardo paints the Mona Lisa
summary: Leonardo da Vinci begins his portrait of Lisa Gherardini; at the same time Michelangelo carves David. The High Renaissance is at its peak.

title: Battle of Agnadello
summary: France crushes the army of Venice, which briefly loses almost all its mainland territory in the War of the League of Cambrai — part of the Italian Wars between France, Spain and the Habsburgs.

title: Sistine Chapel ceiling unveiled
summary: After four years on scaffolding, Michelangelo completes the frescoes of Genesis on the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.

title: Luther's Ninety-five Theses
summary: Martin Luther challenges the sale of indulgences. Spread by the printing press, his ideas launch the Protestant Reformation and split Western Christianity.

title: Ottomans conquer Mamluk Egypt
summary: Selim I defeats the Mamluks at Ridaniya. The Ottomans take Egypt, Syria and the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, and claim the caliphate.

title: Magellan–Elcano circumnavigation
summary: Ferdinand Magellan's Spanish fleet sails west; Magellan is killed in the Philippines, and Juan Sebastián Elcano brings one ship home in 1522 — the first voyage around the world.

title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
summary: Hernán Cortés, with tens of thousands of Indigenous allies and helped by a smallpox epidemic, captures the Aztec capital after a siege of nearly three months.

title: Battle of Mohács
summary: Suleiman the Magnificent destroys the Hungarian army; King Louis II drowns fleeing. Hungary is divided between the Ottomans and the Habsburgs.

title: First Battle of Panipat — Mughal Empire founded
summary: Babur, a Timurid prince from Central Asia, uses cannon and cavalry to defeat the Delhi Sultan Ibrahim Lodi and founds the Mughal Empire.

title: Sack of Rome
summary: Unpaid, mutinous troops of Emperor Charles V sack Rome and imprison the Pope — a traumatic end to the Roman High Renaissance.

title: First Siege of Vienna
summary: Suleiman the Magnificent besieges Vienna but autumn rains and supply problems force him to retreat — the high-water mark of Ottoman power in central Europe.

title: Pizarro captures Atahualpa
summary: Francisco Pizarro's small Spanish force ambushes and captures the Inca emperor Atahualpa, who was fresh from a civil war. He is ransomed for a room of gold, then executed.

title: Henry VIII breaks with Rome
summary: The Act of Supremacy makes the king head of the Church of England after the Pope refuses to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon.

title: Battle of Preveza
summary: Ottoman admiral Hayreddin Barbarossa defeats a Holy League fleet including Venice's galleys; the Ottomans dominate the eastern Mediterranean.

title: Copernicus: the Earth moves around the Sun
summary: Nicolaus Copernicus publishes 'On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres'. Vesalius publishes his anatomy the same year. The Scientific Revolution begins.

title: Silver discovered at Potosí
summary: A mountain of silver is found in the Andes. Mined by forced Indigenous labour, it floods the world with silver — much of it ending up in Ming China.

title: Council of Trent
summary: The Catholic Church's answer to the Reformation: doctrine is clarified, abuses reformed and the Counter-Reformation launched.

title: Ottomans conquer Venetian Cyprus
summary: Selim II invades Cyprus; Nicosia falls in 1570 and Famagusta, after an epic siege, in August 1571. Its commander Marcantonio Bragadin is flayed alive.

title: Battle of Lepanto
summary: The Holy League fleet of Spain, Venice and the Papacy — over 200 galleys, with Venetian galleasses in the front line — destroys the Ottoman fleet in the last great battle of oared ships. Cervantes was wounded aboard.
significance: A huge morale boost for Christian Europe, but Venice still had to cede Cyprus in the peace of 1573; the Ottomans rebuilt their fleet within a year.

title: St Bartholomew's Day massacre
summary: Thousands of French Protestants (Huguenots) are murdered by Catholic mobs in Paris and other cities during France's Wars of Religion.

title: Akbar's Din-i Ilahi and religious tolerance
summary: Mughal emperor Akbar, who abolished the tax on non-Muslims, hosts debates between Muslims, Hindus, Jains, Zoroastrians and Jesuits and promotes a syncretic court cult.

title: Defeat of the Spanish Armada
summary: Philip II's great fleet sent to invade Elizabeth I's England is scattered by English fireships and then wrecked by storms around Scotland and Ireland.

title: Japanese invasions of Korea
summary: Toyotomi Hideyoshi invades Korea; Admiral Yi Sun-sin's 'turtle ships' and Ming Chinese armies eventually force the Japanese out.

title: Battle of Sekigahara
summary: Tokugawa Ieyasu wins the decisive battle of Japan's civil wars. His Tokugawa shogunate keeps Japan peaceful — and largely closed to the world — for 250 years.

title: Dutch East India Company founded
summary: The VOC, the world's first publicly traded company, is chartered two years after the English East India Company. Dutch ships soon dominate the Asian spice trade.

title: Jamestown founded
summary: The first permanent English settlement in North America is founded; Quebec follows in 1608 for France.

title: Galileo's telescope reveals Jupiter's moons
summary: Galileo turns an improved telescope on the sky and discovers Jupiter's moons and the phases of Venus — evidence that the Earth is not the centre of everything.

title: Thirty Years' War begins
summary: The Defenestration of Prague sparks a war that draws in most of Europe and kills perhaps a third of the population of the German lands.

title: The Mayflower reaches New England
summary: English Puritan 'Pilgrims' found Plymouth Colony.

title: Taj Mahal begun
summary: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan begins a white marble mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal; it takes over 20 years to complete.

title: Ming fall; Qing take Beijing
summary: Rebels capture Beijing and the last Ming emperor hangs himself; the Manchus then sweep in and found the Qing dynasty, China's last.

title: Siege of Candia
summary: Venice defends its capital on Crete for 21 years — one of the longest sieges in history — before surrendering the island to the Ottomans in 1669.

title: Peace of Westphalia
summary: The treaties ending the Thirty Years' War recognise Dutch and Swiss independence and the right of rulers to choose their state's religion — often seen as the birth of the modern system of sovereign states.

title: Execution of Charles I
summary: After losing the English Civil War to Parliament, King Charles I is beheaded. England becomes a republic under Oliver Cromwell until 1660.

title: Great Fire of London
summary: A fire in a bakery on Pudding Lane burns for four days and destroys most of the medieval City of London, including St Paul's Cathedral.

title: Newton's Principia
summary: Isaac Newton publishes his laws of motion and universal gravitation, explaining the movements of planets and falling apples with the same mathematics.

title: Battle of Vienna
summary: King Jan III Sobieski of Poland leads the greatest cavalry charge in history to relieve the Ottoman siege of Vienna. The Ottoman tide in Europe turns for good.

title: Venetian shell blows up the Parthenon
summary: During Francesco Morosini's Venetian conquest of the Morea, a mortar round ignites Ottoman gunpowder stored in the Parthenon, wrecking the 2,100-year-old temple.

title: Glorious Revolution
summary: James II is ousted by his Dutch son-in-law William of Orange. The Bill of Rights (1689) establishes parliamentary supremacy in England.

title: Peter the Great founds St Petersburg
summary: Peter I builds a new capital on the Baltic as his 'window on Europe', part of his drive to modernise Russia.

title: Battle of Poltava
summary: Peter the Great crushes Charles XII's Swedish army; Russia replaces Sweden as the great power of northern Europe.

title: Peace of Utrecht
summary: The War of the Spanish Succession ends: a Bourbon keeps the Spanish throne, but Britain gains Gibraltar and Minorca and emerges as a great power.

title: Nader Shah sacks Delhi
summary: The Persian ruler Nader Shah defeats the Mughals at Karnal, sacks Delhi and carries off the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

title: Lisbon earthquake
summary: A huge earthquake, tsunami and fire destroy Lisbon on All Saints' Day, killing tens of thousands and shaking Enlightenment thinkers' faith in a benevolent order.

title: Battle of Plassey
summary: Robert Clive's East India Company troops, helped by bribery, defeat the Nawab of Bengal — the start of British rule in India.

title: Seven Years' War
summary: Often called the first world war: Britain and Prussia fight France, Austria and Russia across five continents. Britain wins Canada and dominance in India.

title: Watt's steam engine goes to work
summary: James Watt's much more efficient steam engine with a separate condenser starts working in mines and mills — an engine of the Industrial Revolution.

title: US Declaration of Independence
summary: Thirteen British colonies declare themselves independent, asserting that 'all men are created equal' with rights to 'life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness'.

title: Cook lands at Botany Bay
summary: James Cook charts the east coast of Australia and claims it for Britain; the First Fleet of convicts arrives in 1788.

title: Siege of Yorktown
summary: A Franco-American army traps Lord Cornwallis' British force, effectively winning the American Revolutionary War.

title: Storming of the Bastille
summary: Parisians storm the royal fortress-prison. The French Revolution abolishes feudal privileges, proclaims the Rights of Man and, in 1792, the Republic.

title: Haitian Revolution
summary: Enslaved Africans in France's richest colony rise up. Led by Toussaint Louverture, they abolish slavery and in 1804 found Haiti, the first Black republic.

title: Execution of Louis XVI
summary: The deposed king is guillotined; the Reign of Terror follows.

title: Fall of the Republic of Venice
summary: Threatened by Napoleon's army, the Great Council votes the 1,100-year-old Republic out of existence. Ludovico Manin, the 120th and last doge, abdicates.
significance: By the Treaty of Campo Formio that October, Napoleon hands Venice to Austria.

title: Rosetta Stone found
summary: French soldiers in Napoleon's Egyptian campaign find a decree in Greek, Demotic and hieroglyphs; Champollion uses it to decipher hieroglyphs in 1822.

title: Ahmad Shah Durrani founds Afghanistan
summary: After Nader Shah's assassination, Ahmad Shah Durrani is chosen leader by the Afghan tribes and founds the Durrani Empire, the basis of modern Afghanistan.

title: Qing take Taiwan
summary: The Kangxi Emperor's fleet defeats the Ming loyalist Kingdom of Tungning and annexes Taiwan; Qing China reaches its zenith under Kangxi and Qianlong.
